steps.action: Call your bank now and say you were tricked into sending a bank transfer. Ask them to stop any transactions and ask what else you should do.
Report the scam to Scamwatch. You can also report it to the police online through ReportCyber.

If your bank does not help, make a formal complaint to the bank. If you are still unhappy, contact the Australian Financial Complaints Authority. It is free. Do it within 2 years of the bank's reply. You can also complain about the bank that received the money.

evidence.quote: Contact your bank or card provider immediately to report the scam.
Ask them to stop any transactions and ask what other action you should take.
You can also make an official report to the police online.
You can make a complaint against your bank, or a receiving bank
you should complain to us within two years of getting this response
Most obligations will apply from 31 March 2027

extra.notes: No scam-reimbursement law or cap is in force yet: the Scams Prevention Framework's main obligations, and AFCA's role under it, start 31 March 2027, and its codes are still being drafted. AFCA time limit is 2 years from the bank's internal-dispute reply or 6 years from becoming aware of the loss, whichever comes first; kept in the action text with deadlineDays null because the app renders days. Police report is via ReportCyber (https://www.cyber.gov.au/submit-a-report). Scamwatch names IDCARE (1800 595 160) for identity help; omitted as a step because IDCARE is a not-for-profit, not a government body.

steps.action: Call your card provider now and say you were tricked into paying by card. Ask them to stop any transactions and ask for a chargeback.
steps.contact: the number on the back of your card

steps.action: Report the scam to Scamwatch. You can also report it to the police online through ReportCyber.
If your card provider says no, make a formal complaint to them. If you are still unhappy, contact the Australian Financial Complaints Authority. It is free. Do it within 2 years of their reply.

evidence.quote: Contact your bank or card provider immediately to report the scam.
They may be able to give you a chargeback.
You can also make an official report to the police online.
you should complain to us within two years of getting this response

extra.notes: Chargeback is a card-scheme process; no official AU page fetched states a chargeback deadline, so none is set and the step says 'now'. No card-specific scam refund law. AFCA time limit kept in the action text (deadlineDays null). Police report via ReportCyber (https://www.cyber.gov.au/submit-a-report).
